newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - SEPT 26.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - SEPT 26.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- The government is likely to discuss at today's session the draft state and social security budgets and plans about the judiciary reform.

- The state secretary of the Ministry of agriculture criticised the Finance Ministry for the low level of agricultural subsidies planned for 1997. This could aggravate recession in the agricultural sector, he said.
- Prime Minister Horn Gyula answered the invitation of Jozsef Torgyan, President of the Smallholder's Party (FKgP), for a television debate, saying it is out of time as there is no election campaign.
- The Sarvar sugar factory's sugar beet procession campaign has been cancelled because the harvest is delayed by heavy rains. The beets are growing, but sugar content is decreasing.
- Veszprem local municipality takes a legal action against the state privatisation agency APV, saying it lost profits because APV failed to transfer due properties of the town to Veszprem.
- An international conference began on Thursday on the role of Hungary's 1956 revolution in world politics.
